slider.heading: Usage
Format options
Range Slider Anatomy
slider.description: v3 builds a range slider from its parts: a `Label`, an `Output`, and a `Track` whose render prop is handed the state so it can draw one `Thumb` per value. The `thumb` closure is that render prop.
slider.code:
gpui::div()
    .w(px(320.))
    .child(Slider::new("slider-anatomy", 25.)
                .default_values([25., 75.])
                .label("Price range")
                .show_value(true)
                .thumb(|index, value| {
                    gpui::div()
                        .id(("sl-anatomy-thumb", index))
                        .size(px(18.))
                        .rounded_full()
                        .border_2()
                        .border_color(gpui::white())
                        .bg(gpui::rgb(0x0085F5))
                        // The closure is handed the value the slider
                        // already computed for this thumb, so the
                        // caller never re-derives it.
                        .flex()
                        .items_center()
                        .justify_center()
                        .child(
                            gpui::div()

table.heading: Selection

Virtualization
table.description: v3 wraps the table in `Virtualizer` with `TableLayout`. Cells here are built elements, which cannot be handed out twice, so a virtual table takes a row factory and asks for the rows the viewport shows — one thousand of them, forty pixels each.
table.code:
gpui::div()
    .flex()
    .flex_col()
    .items_start()
    .gap(px(12.))
    .children(vec![
        Table::new(vec![])
            .id("table-virtualization")
            .column(TableColumn::new("Name").is_row_header(true))
            .column("Email")
            .row_height(px(40.))
            .max_h(px(320.))
            .virtual_rows(
                1000,
                "virtual-users",
                |i| i.to_string().into(),
                |i| {
                    let (name, email) = virtual_user(i);
                    TableRow::new(vec![
                        gpui::div().child(name).into_any_element(),
                        gpui::div().child(email).into_any_element(),
                    ])
                },
            )
            .virtual_text_value(|i| virtual_user(i).0.into())
            .into_any_element(),
        para(
            "`estimated_row_height` virtualizes rows that differ: gpui's \
                                 `list` measures each one it builds, and `loader_height` \
                                 fixes the load-more row underneath.",
            cx,
        ),
        Table::new(vec![])
            .id("table-virtual-var")
            .column(TableColumn::new("Name").is_row_header(true))
            .column("Email")
            .estimated_row_height(px(44.))
            .loader_height(px(44.))
            .max_h(px(320.))
            .is_pending(true)
            .virtual_rows(
                1000,
                "virtual-variable-users",
                |i| i.to_string().into(),
                |i| {
                    let (name, email) = virtual_user(i);
                    let mut cells = vec![gpui::div()
                        .flex()
                        .flex_col()
                        .child(name)
                        .when(i % 3 == 0, |el| {
                            el.child(
                                gpui::div()
                                    .text_size(px(12.))
                                    .child("Signed up this week"),
                            )
                        })
                        .into_any_element()];
                    cells.push(gpui::div().child(email).into_any_element());
                    TableRow::new(cells)
                },
            )
            .virtual_text_value(|i| virtual_user(i).0.into())
            .into_any_element(),
    ])

form.heading: Server Errors
form.description: `validationErrors` is HeroUI's `ValidationErrors` record — server errors keyed by field name, `Record<string, string | string[]>`. The Form routes each name into that field's own error slot: editing a field clears only its message while its sibling keeps theirs, Reset hides them all, and a re-render that passes the same record re-arms nothing. New response supplies a genuinely new record — identical content, fresh identity — so both messages re-arm.

typography.description: `Prose` provides only the `text-foreground` color. GPUI has no per-tag CSS selectors, so the per-tag descendant styles in v3's `.typography-prose` — `h1`–`h6`, `p`, `code`, `a`, lists — cannot be inherited; children must already be semantic elements.
typography.imports:
use herogpui::prelude::{ParagraphSize, Prose, Typography, TypographyType};
use gpui::prelude::*;
typography.code:
Prose::new()
    .child(Typography::paragraph(
        ParagraphSize::Base,
        "A paragraph inside `Prose` carries its own body metrics.",
    ))

typography.heading: Scale
typography.code:
gpui::div()
    .flex()
    .flex_col()
    .items_start()
    .gap(px(12.))
    .children(scale
        .iter()
        .map(|(kind, name, meta)| {
            gpui::div()
                .flex()
                .items_center()
                .gap(px(24.))
                .child(
                    gpui::div()
                        .w(px(110.))
                        .flex()
                        .flex_col()
                        .child(
                            gpui::div()
                                .text_size(px(13.))
                                .font_weight(gpui::FontWeight::SEMIBOLD)
                                .child(name.to_string()),
                        )
                        .child(
                            gpui::div()
                                .text_size(px(11.))
                                .text_color(muted)
                                .child(meta.to_string()),
                        ),
                )
                .child(
                    Typography::new("Build better interfaces").kind(*kind),
                )
        })
        )

typography.heading: Colors & weights
typography.code:
gpui::div()
    .flex()
    .flex_col()
    .items_start()
    .gap(px(12.))
    .children(vec![
        Typography::new("Default foreground").into_any_element(),
        Typography::new("Muted foreground")
            .color(TextColor::Muted)
            .into_any_element(),
        Typography::new("Bold body")
            .weight(FontWeight::Bold)
            .into_any_element(),
    ])

typography.heading: Alignment & truncation
typography.code:
gpui::div()
    .flex()
    .flex_col()
    .items_start()
    .gap(px(12.))
    .children(vec![
        Typography::new("Centered against the measure")
            .align(TextAlign::Center)
            .into_any_element(),
        Typography::new("Aligned to the end")
            .align(TextAlign::End)
            .into_any_element(),
        Typography::new(
            "Justify falls back to start alignment: gpui has no text-justify.",
        )
        .align(TextAlign::Justify)
        .into_any_element(),
        gpui::div()
            .w(px(220.))
            .child(
                Typography::new(
                    "A long line that truncates to a single ellipsis at the \
                                         edge of its 220px box instead of wrapping.",
                )
                .truncate(true),
            )
            .into_any_element(),
    ])

typography.heading: Primitives
typography.code:
gpui::div()
    .flex()
    .flex_col()
    .items_start()
    .gap(px(12.))
    .children(vec![
        Typography::heading(3, "Dashboard").into_any_element(),
        Typography::paragraph(
            ParagraphSize::Base,
            "Paragraph supports base, sm and xs sizes.",
        )
        .into_any_element(),
        Typography::code("cargo add herogpui").into_any_element(),
    ])
